_doc: G-6 ANTI-VACUITY REGISTRY — every scanner check ships a proof that it CAN fail.
Each gate names a check and one or more DEFECTS. For each defect the runner:
1. CONTROL — asserts the check is GREEN on the pristine tree,
2. PLANT   — applies the mutation to a SCRATCH copy and asserts it changed something,
3. ORACLE  — runs an INDEPENDENT command proving the planted defect is really there,
4. DEFEAT  — demands the check go RED. If it stays green, it is DECORATION and CI fails.
The ORACLE is not ceremony. Without it, 'my fixture was bogus' and 'the check is blind'
produce byte-identical output — and conflating those two is the entire bug class (CR-65).
Defect ops:  write {path: content} | delete [paths] | replace [{path, pattern, replace}]
The 'oracle' is a bash command run from the scratch tree root; exit 0 = defect confirmed present.

gates.title: No process.exit() in library code
gates.guards: library modules must not kill the host process; only CLI entrypoints may exit
gates._canary_doc: THE RUNNER'S OWN ANTI-VACUITY PROOF. Check 3 is a known-GOOD gate: plant a process.exit() and it genuinely goes RED. If THIS gate ever reports 'decoration', the defect is in the RUNNER, not the check — and the runner must abort rather than report a tree full of false positives. This is not paranoia: the first version of the runner keyed on 'FAIL: Check N', matched nothing (most checks don't name themselves in their failure text), and called this working gate decoration. A harness that reports EVERYTHING as broken is as useless as one that reports nothing as broken — and it fails in the more believable direction.

gates.title: Knowledge system uses getCodeGraphDb()
gates.guards: no direct SQLite opens outside the accessor modules (db.ts / memory-db.ts)
gates._known_defect: T-1 — this check's regex 'sqlite3\(' is an unbalanced paren in a BRE. Real grep exits 1 with 'parentheses not balanced'; stderr is swallowed by 2>/dev/null; the count is 0; the check reports PASS. It has NEVER run.

gates.title: Auto-learning tier-gate wiring (CR-54 / VR-AUTO-LEARNING-TIER)
gates.guards: the auto-learning promotion chokepoint actually CALLS the tier gate
gates._known_defect: T-3 — this check greps for the bare identifier 'assertAutoLearningEntitled'. A COMMENT satisfies it. In the real incident the gate was deleted from production code, the identifier survived in a comment, and Check 30 reported 'tier-gate wiring intact'.

replace.replace: // [anti-vacuity probe] gate removed; identifier survives only here: assertAutoLearningEntitled

gates.title: Memory integrity invariants (CR-61)
gates.guards: sub-check (g): the render key is never readable from the environment — whoever sets that env var can forge every authorship stamp
gates._known_defect: T-2 — sub-check (g) pipes 'grep -q' into 'grep -qv'. '-q' is QUIET and prints nothing, so the right-hand grep always reads EMPTY stdin and always exits non-zero. The condition CANNOT be true.
